title: Commutative and Associative Properties
h1: Order and grouping, put to work
_notes: Source of truth for the 0.2.1 practice set. Kinds: "num" (default; same as 0.1, the answer is a number), "expr" (the answer is an expression: a = answer, a_read = how it is said; every line and option is checked at several values of the variables; each wrong option has read = how it is said) and "name" (which property an identity shows: show/say/notes are one block each, ⟨…⟩ in show is highlighted; wrong = the other two properties). Implied multiplication (3x, 2(x + 1), x(x + 5)) and · are allowed. Chips: COMM blue, ASSOC purple, DIST yellow, CALC green, REWRITE white. Also "multi" (select all that apply) and "match" (match pairs): see docs/exercises.md.

exercises.read: Seven plus nine equals nine plus seven.
say: The same two numbers are on both sides. Only their order changed: the seven and the nine traded places.
Both sides equal sixteen. Changing the order is the commutative property.

wrong.why: Associative is about grouping with parentheses. There are no parentheses here.
wrong.say: there are no parentheses being moved

wrong.why: Distributive needs a number multiplied by a sum, like 3(x + 2).

exercises.read: The quantity six times five, times two, equals six times the quantity five times two.
say: The numbers are in the same order on both sides: six, five, two. What moved are the parentheses.
Thirty times two is sixty, and six times ten is also sixty. Regrouping is the associative property.

wrong.why: The numbers did not trade places: 6, 5, 2 is the same order on both sides.
wrong.say: the numbers stay in the same order

wrong.why: Distributive spreads a multiplication over a sum. Here everything is multiplication.
wrong.say: there is no sum inside the parentheses

exercises.prompt: Use the properties to find the value.
say: Twenty-five and four make one hundred, so let's put them together. The commutative property lets us swap the thirteen and the four.
The associative property lets us group the twenty-five with the four.
Twenty-five times four is one hundred.
One hundred times thirteen is one thousand three hundred.

wrong.why: You added 25 and 4 instead of multiplying them.
You added the 13 instead of multiplying by it.
wrong.say: add the thirteen at the end

exercises.read: x times eight equals eight x.
say: Eight x means eight times x. So both sides multiply the same two things, in a different order.
Swapping the order of a multiplication is the commutative property. That's why we can always write the number first.

wrong.why: There is only one multiplication, so there is nothing to regroup.
There is no sum for the 8 to be spread over.
wrong.say: there is no sum to spread over

exercises.read: Three plus the quantity x plus seven equals the quantity three plus x, plus seven.
say: Read each side from left to right: three, x, seven. The order didn't change.
Only the parentheses moved. Changing the grouping is the associative property.

wrong.why: It looks like something moved, but the order is the same: 3, x, 7. Only the parentheses moved.
wrong.say: the terms stay in the same order

wrong.why: Nothing multiplies the parentheses; it's all addition.

exercises.prompt: Select all the identities that show the associative property.
exercises.read: Which of these show the associative property? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: So two of them show the associative property: the numbers stay in the same order, and only the grouping changes.

options.why: Same order, the parentheses moved: associative.
options.say: Four plus seven, then plus three, equals four plus the quantity seven plus three. The order stays the same. Only the parentheses moved. That is associative.

options.why: The terms swapped places: that is commutative.
options.say: Six plus y equals y plus six. The terms swap places. That is commutative, not associative.

options.why: Same order of factors, new grouping: associative.
options.say: Two times the quantity five times x equals the quantity two times five, times x. Same order, new grouping. Associative.

options.why: The parentheses stayed put; x and 2 swapped inside them: commutative.
options.say: Careful with this one. The parentheses did not move. Inside them, x and two swapped places. That is commutative.
Three times the quantity x plus one equals three x plus three. That multiplies across a sum. It is distributive.

exercises.read: Five times the quantity two times x equals the quantity five times two, times x.
say: There are parentheses next to a number, but look inside. There is no sum, only multiplication.
The factors keep their order: five, two, x. Only the grouping changed. That's the associative property, and both sides are ten x.

wrong.why: Distributive needs a sum inside, like 5(2 + x). Here it's 2 · x, a product.
wrong.say: there is no sum inside the parentheses

wrong.why: The order is the same on both sides: 5, 2, x.
wrong.say: the factors stay in the same order

exercises.prompt: Match each identity with the property it shows.
exercises.read: Match each identity with the property it shows.
exercises.say_answer: Order changes mean commutative. Grouping changes mean associative.

pairs.say: Eight times five equals five times eight. The factors swap places, so it is commutative.
The quantity a plus b, plus four, equals a plus the quantity b plus four. Same order, the parentheses moved. Associative.

pairs.why: The parentheses stayed; y and 1 swapped inside.
pairs.say: Seven plus the quantity y plus one equals seven plus the quantity one plus y. The parentheses stay where they are. Inside, y and one swap. Commutative.

pairs.why: Same order of factors, new grouping.
pairs.say: x times the quantity three times two equals the quantity x times three, times two. Same order, new grouping. Associative.

exercises.prompt: Use the properties to find the value.
say: Four and twenty-five make one hundred, but they're far apart. Swap the thirty-seven and the twenty-five.
Now group the four with the twenty-five.
Four times twenty-five is one hundred.
One hundred times thirty-seven is three thousand seven hundred.

wrong.why: You added 4 and 25 instead of multiplying them.
You added the 37 instead of multiplying by it.

exercises.read: The quantity x plus three, times two, equals two times the quantity x plus three.
say: There is a sum in parentheses, so distributive is tempting. But the two is not multiplied into the terms.
Two factors, the quantity and the two, just traded places. That's the commutative property.

wrong.why: Distributing would give 2x + 6. Here the parentheses stay; the 2 just moved to the front.
wrong.say: the two is not multiplied into the parentheses

wrong.why: Associative regroups three or more things. Here two factors just swapped.
